newsitem.title: ITALY: Enterprise sees Italy oil find 10-20 bln bls.
newsitem.headline: Enterprise sees Italy oil find 10-20 bln bls.

text.p: Britain's Enterprise Oil Plc said it sees the potential of oil reserves in the southern Italian Val d'Agri area, in the Basilicata region, at around 10-20 billion barrels.

The group's managing director Pierre Jungels said in an interview in Milan's financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore on Friday that the potential of the Val d'Agri oilfield "is between 10 and 20 billion barrels".
"We have found the largest deposit of onshore oil in western Europe," Jungels was quoted as saying in the paper.
Simon Oddie, Enterprise general manager in Rome, told Reuters difficult geology in the region could mean that at best 50 percent of the oil in place would be recovered.
"Recovery has some uncertainty but we would expect it to be in the 10-50 percent range," he said.
Jungels added that more accurate data on the potential of the area would be available towards the end of the year.
When a pipeline to the southern port and refinery of Taranto is completed in 1999, production could easily reach 100,000 barrels per day (bpd).

Enterprise is in partnership with Italy's oil giant ENI production arm Agip in exploring the southern Italian area and the estimate for the field's size helped push up ENI's share price on the Milan stock market.
At 0940 GMT, ENI's share price was up 1.85 percent at 9,075 lire in a slightly firmer Italian bourse.
Britain's Lasmo L is also a partner.
Oddie said Enterprise was currently producing about 8,000 bpd in southern Italy. The oil is being trucked by road to Taranto.
